items.title: UBTree: parallel tree drafting gives about 3.4x faster decoding for Ling-3.0, with drafters released on Hugging Face
items.summary: A unigram proposer suggests candidate tokens and a bigram selector links them into a draft tree built fully in parallel. On Ling-3.0-flash (124B) with 4 GPUs it reports about 1,010 output tokens per second at concurrency 1, a 3.43x average end-to-end speedup over plain decoding across six benchmarks. Drafters for Ling-3.0-tiny-8B and Ling-3.0-flash-124B are out now, with more promised.

items.title: Ling-3.0-flash on a single DGX Spark: decode up 42.5% (37.8 to 53.9 tok/s) after NVIDIA-assisted tuning
items.summary: Ant Ling and NVIDIA applied three inference optimizations to the open-weight Ling-3.0-flash on one DGX Spark. Over 1,319 GSM8K questions, decode throughput rose 42.5% and mean latency fell 24.5% (15.2 s to 11.5 s) with no measurable accuracy change. Useful as a reference for running a large open MoE on the Spark.

items.title: tinygrad tinybox red kimi: Kimi K3 at home at 40 tok/s interactive for $30k
items.summary: A new tinybox build aimed at running the Kimi K3 frontier model locally. A follow-up diagram shows tinygrad driving the NVMe drives directly from the AMD GPUs, so weights that do not fit in GPU memory stream from disk.

doubt.pushback: Replies ask for a benchmark, the quantization used, and whether 40 tok/s is single-session or aggregate; none answered. One reply could not find it on the site yet.

items.title: DCOCO: a light corrector fixes inconsistent parallel drafts in speculative decoding, up to 6.6x faster
items.summary: Parallel drafting proposes several tokens at once but they do not know which earlier tokens were accepted. DCOCO scores token combinations in parallel with a small corrector, reporting up to 6.6x faster decoding than standard generation on four LLMs and 8-19% more throughput than other speculative methods.

items.title: Looped Prediction Transformer: sharing one KV cache across loops cuts context memory up to 79% and improves perplexity
items.summary: Instead of a separate KV cache per loop, the first loop builds a shared cache and later loops keep only a small window of their own. Across 150M to 1B models it improves perplexity and accuracy; at 1B the hybrid has 10% lower perplexity than a standard Transformer, though at much higher inference compute.

items.title: Amp adds macOS Satellites: agents spawn Macs on demand to build, test and run iOS and macOS apps
items.summary: Amp agents can now start a Mac to build and test Apple-platform apps. Amp's Quinn Slack says they measured that even macOS-heavy work needs a Mac only about 35% of the time, so the Mac is attached only when needed, which makes it faster and cheaper.

items.title: tracekit for Hermes Agent: tool calls are allowed, blocked or held for approval before they run, with a tamper-evident run log
items.summary: A community plugin by Cygnux Labs. In a scripted test, ls was allowed, a download piped into a shell was blocked, and a remote branch delete waited for approval. Editing the run file afterward to mark the blocked call as allowed made the log check fail at that record.

items.title: OpenBMB ForgeKernel tops the FIB track of NVIDIA's SOL Bench and Huawei's CANNBench, now live-optimizing a DeepSeek MLA kernel
items.summary: OpenBMB's self-improving kernel agent writes GPU kernels from math and hardware limits alone, without reference code. It is streaming an attempt to beat expert implementations of DeepSeek V4.1's MLA kernel, with a public results page.

security_forwarded.matched: always_forward: agent tooling. (1) IBM bulletin for Langflow 1.0.0 to 1.12.2: two unauthenticated 9.8 RCEs, CVE-2026-104334 (GHSA-74xw-7rg4-6p4c, code injection) and CVE-2026-93674 (GHSA-xhw9-mf2x-qh4j, OS command injection), plus sandbox escape, path traversal and credential exposure; fix is 1.12.3, which supersedes the 1.10.3 advice from 2026-10-28. (2) mcp-remote 0.1.32 to 0.1.38 SSRF during OAuth (CVE-2026-51994, GHSA-8rrr-xx35-4q6h, critical): a malicious MCP server can make it fetch localhost, LAN or cloud metadata URLs; used to connect Claude Desktop, Cursor or Windsurf to remote MCP servers. Both verified in the GitHub advisory database. Neither Langflow nor mcp-remote is installed on the box; neither is in stack.json, so fleet use is unknown.
